name: roc_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Rate of Change (ROC) over 20 bars on 1-min data measures the percentage price change over the last 20 minutes. When ROC(20) exceeds its 95th percentile for that stock's intraday distribution (computed over the last 5 sessions), it signals an abnormally strong momentum burst. Unlike fixed thresholds, using percentile-based ROC adapts to each stock's volatility profile. The edge exists because these extreme ROC events often correspond to institutional block executions or algorithmic momentum-chasing that creates a self-reinforcing trend for the next 15-30 minutes. The inefficiency persists because computing per-stock ROC percentiles in real-time requires historical intraday data infrastructure that most retail traders lack.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND has at least 5 prior sessions of 1-min data

long.confirmation: ROC_20 remains above 90th percentile for 2 consecutive bars (sustained momentum, not one-bar spike)

short.confirmation: ROC_20 remains below 10th percentile for 2 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market order on 2nd consecutive extreme-percentile bar close

exit.stop_loss: 0.2% from entry (tight stop — if momentum fades quickly, thesis is wrong)
exit.signal_exit: exit if ROC_pctile drops below 50 (momentum normalized)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; increase to 1.5L if ROC_pctile > 99 (extreme outlier momentum)

filters.vix_filter: no specific filter — extreme ROC can occur in any VIX regime
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:30 (need time for momentum to play out)
filters.volume_filter: volume surge > 2x essential — filters out low-volume noise spikes
filters.event_filter: check if ROC spike is news-driven — may continue (good) or be a one-time pop (bad)
other_filters: requires 5 prior sessions of intraday data for percentile computation

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — percentile-based ROC thresholds are adaptive and not commonly used at this timeframe

weaknesses: Momentum chasing after extreme ROC can lead to buying the top — the spike may be a one-bar outlier event (news, block deal)
The 2-bar confirmation delay means entering after significant price movement; risk/reward may already be degraded
Per-stock percentile calculation requires maintaining 5 days of 1-min data per stock — significant data management overhead
prior_art: Rate of Change is a basic momentum indicator. Percentile-based thresholds are used in quantile regression and momentum factor research (Jegadeesh & Titman, 1993 for daily). Intraday ROC percentiles are less documented. The volume confirmation requirement draws from Blitz & Vliet (2008) 'Momentum Factor' research on volume-confirmed momentum.
notes: Edge math: 0.50 * 50bps - 0.50 * 28bps = 25 - 14 = 11 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 0 bps. Breakeven on paper. The trailing stop should capture outlier winners (>0.5%) that pull the average up. If avg winner expands to 60bps with trailing: 0.50*60 - 0.50*28 = 16 bps gross, net ~5 bps. Viable with trailing stop optimization.
